newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ODDS WEIGH AGAINST HEARTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ODDS WEIGH AGAINST HEARTS.

text.p: Confident Scottish champions Rangers head into Saturday's clash with Hearts 12 points clear at the top of the premier division while their opponents, already the clear underdogs, are battling against poor form and a burgeoning injury crisis.

Rangers, aiming to equal the record of arch-rivals Celtic this season by claiming their ninth consecutive Scottish league title, have shown few signs of vulnerability this season, winning 13 of their first 17 games and scoring 42 goals in the process.
The most intruiging decision Rangers' manager Walter Smith has to make for Saturday's match is up front, where goalscoring legend Ally McCoist has been suffering a light ankle injury.
He started on the bench in Rangers' midweek win over Kilmarnock opening up a place in the starting 11 for Erik Bo Andersen, out of the side for much of the season.
The big Dane took his chance, scoring a hat-trick in Rangers' 4-2 win, and has no intention of dropping back on to the substitutes' bench.

"I will always be there to take chances and I have scored many hat-tricks before," said Andersen, hinting to Smith he is ready for another full 90 minutes on Saturday. "I need to be playing regularly and if I get a game I think I will get better over the season."
Rangers' do have long-term injuries, most notably to Scotland forward Gordon Durie who will be out until at least the middle of January with a hamstring strain.

But their strength-in-depth has allowed them to clock up 41 points from 17 games, 12 more than second-placed Aberdeen and 20 more than Hearts, who looked disjointed in losing their last two matches -- 2-1 at home to Aberdeen and then 2-0 at bottom-of-the-table Kilmarnock.

"It was a dreadful performance and what makes it worse is that we played better after we went a goal behind," Hearts manager Jim Jefferies said after the Kilmarnock match. "We missed several good opportunities and the quality of our crosses into the box was dreadful."
To make matters worse, Hearts, with nothing like the strength in depth of their Glasgow rivals, have a growing casualty list.
Former Rangers player Dave McPherson is still a long term absentee, as is ex-AC Milan midfielder Stefano Salvatori.
Paul Ritchie, former Manchester City striker Darren Beckford, Neil McCann and new signing Jim Hamilton are also now doubtful after picking up injuries in recent weeks.

Nothing better illustrates the current fortunes of the two sides than the seven-month stories of Rangers' Alan McClaren and Hearts' captain Gary Locke, neither of whom, before this week, had played for their clubs since last season's Scottish Cup final, when Rangers hammered Hearts 5-1.
McClaren, who has had surgery on an injured right knee, played his comeback match on Tuesday, helping the champions to a 4-2 victory over Kilmarnock.
He came through it unscathed and could reclaim his place in the back line, ousting Yugoslav-born Gordan Petric, although Smith has expressed doubts about McClaren's match fitness.

Locke, who was stretchered off the pitch in that eventful cup final with a serious knee ligament injury, had hoped to return this week but his comeback has been delayed and he will definitely miss out on Saturday's big clash.

The Edinburgh side will take heart from their two league victories against Rangers in the second half of last season, especially their 3-0 win at Ibrox in January. Given that Rangers lost only three league matches all season, Hearts can be proud of that record.
But when it has mattered, in the cup final in May and in this season's League Cup final, Rangers have demonstrated their ability to raise their game high enough to beat any team in Scotland.
